newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Aug 15.

text.p: Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a surprise decision last night by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, the Federal Government will allow the key shareholder in Optus Communications, United Kingdom company Cable & Wireless, to take control of the company. The move clears the way for the proposed A$4 billion public float of Optus. Page 1.

The key shareholders in Ansett Worldwide Aviation Services, News Corp Ltd, and TNT's parent company KPN, look like abandoning plans to undertake a securitisation package for the aircraft-leasing venture and may offload the group to either a United States syndicate, or to GE Capital Corp. Page 39.

AMP Society chief executive George Trumball said yesterday the Australian Stock Exchange has granted initial approval for the restriction of 5 per cent maximum individual shareholding limits for a five year period, a move that extends the group's protectin from takeover, and has been the preference of policy holders. Page 39.

Construction company Leighton Holdings Ltd announced an abnormal net profit of A$46 million from asset sales, which lifted its net profit for 1996-97 to A$132.1 million, almost double its previous result. The announcement saw shares in the compny lift almost 6 per cent yesterday. Page 39.

BHP chief executive officer John Prescott said on ABC-TV's Lateline program last night that BHP chairman Jerry Ellis would not have known that one-quarter of his stake in the Big Australian has been sold just prior to the announcements of the resignations of three top executives in the company. Page 40.

Colonial Ltd chief executive Peter Smedley said yesterday the company's strong maiden interim profit of A$118 million was the result of large cost reductions and solid new business growth. The result was ahead of market expectations, and should see the grop topple its prospectus forecast of A$180 million in earnings in its first year. Page 40
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following yesterday's High Court ruling that declared the former Federal Government confiscated Newcrest Mining's rights for Coronation Hill without paying just terms of compensation under the Constitution, mining at the sacred site in the Northern Territry could go ahead, as may a compensation claim by miners. Page 25.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello last night overturned his own foreign ownership restrictions on the telecommunications sector, a move that will allow Optus Communications' foreign shareholder Cable and Wireless to cement its control by increasing its stae to 49 per cent. Page 25.

The Australian Stock Exchange's listing committee has allowed the AMP Society to set a 5 per cent shareholding limit for five years, which should protect it from takeover after it lists next year. The move has been criticised by AMP Policyholders Associaion chairman Patrick Roe, who described it as "extraordinary" and "unparalleled". Page 25.

The chairman of South Australian wine maker Normans Wines, Lionel Krongold, says the company is set to increase its growth through overseas exports after reporting a A$1.1 million turnaround into profitability. Growth in export turnover of 82 per cent has been achieved, and the company has enjoyed a 25 per cent increase in domestic case sales. Page 27.

EconTech director Chris Murphy, and Access Economics director Chris Richardson said yesterday businesses should look carefully at the fine print of any new tax mix reforms before supporting a goods and services tax. Murphy said the car industry would benfit from such as tax, but the service sector could finish up worse off. Page 27.

BHP Petroleum and Petroz have announced encouraging results from the Layang-1 exploration well that they are working on with partners Santos and Inpex Sahul. The well's hydrocarbon shows are pointing to a possible expansion of the Elang-Kakatua project in the future. Page 27.

Casino's hopes up for high-roller tax break Sydney Harbour Casino chairman Dick Warburton indicated yesterday negotiations with the New South Wales Government are on track when he said the Casino hopes to secure a lower tax rate for international high-rollers next month, which should increase earnigs performance after poor results for the six months to June. Page 25.

Despite receiving approval from the Australian Stock Exchange to cap individual shareholders to owning just 5 per cent of the company for five years after it demutualises, the AMP Society said the move does mean it is takeover proof. The approval came in response to the requests of policyholders who feared a takeover would be detrimental to their benefits. Page 25.

Several highly profitable share investments, and a strong performance from MLC, have boosted property and financial services group Lend Lease Corporation to its 22nd consecutive annual profit rise. This year's figures of A$322 million for the year to Jun were up 15 per cent from last year. Page 25.

Australian Football League chief executive Wayne Jackson yesterday met with James Packer and David Leckie from the Nine Network yesterday morning, before meeting with representatives from the Seven Network in the afternoon, as negotiations for the lucrative AFL television rights after 2001 intensified. Page 25.

The Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia executive director Susan Ryan yesterday gave the peak lobby group's support for the Federal Government's controversial super fund member choice policy that will be introduced in steps from July 1998. Page 27.

Burswood Property Trust yesterday announced a net profit for the year to June 30 of A$42.42 million, a lift from last year's profit of A$38.73 million. The trust said the second half of 1996-97 suffered lower gaming revenue and profitability than the secnd half of the fiscal year. Page 27.
THE AGE

Colonial Group has recorded success in its shift from a mutual society to a listed company with yesterday's announcement of an interim result of A$118 million, a figure that well exceed market expectations and puts the group on line for blasting of its prspectus forecasts. Page B1.

The Federal Government announced yesterday foreign investment regulations have been lifted for telecommunications groups Optus and Vodafone, a move it hopes will allow competition to thrive. The move will generally mean that foreign shareholders will be able to buy as much of an Australian telecommunications company as they want. Page B1.

Luxury car and paint group Lanes looks set to be taken over by South African industrial conglomerate Barlow, a move that will see shares in Lanes acquired by Barlow's Australian arm for A$3.42 each. The move will also give Barlow the right to retained th fully franked dividend of about eight cents a share. Page B1.

Lend Lease has delivered its 22nd consecutive increase in net profit with a 15 per cent rise to A$322 million for the 12 months to June 30. The property and financial services group's managing director David Higgins believes increase profit should be posed again next year. Page B3.

After announcing an 88 per cent increase in annual profit to A$132 million, Leighton Holdings chief executive Wal King said yesterday that with A$500 million sitting in its war chest, the company will review its operations and consider a possible expansio into South America. Page B3.

Sydney Harbour Casino chairman Dick Warburton is confident the group can overcome its looses and negotiate a lower tax rate deal that would bring it into line with the major casinos in Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth. SHC is applying to the New South WalesGovernment to have the tax on international gamblers loosened from 22 per cent to 10 per cent. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
